recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中央有一顆遠大於周圍顆粒球系細胞的大型腫瘤細胞，細胞質灰藍且布滿大小不一的透明空泡，核大、染色質粗糙並有核仁，旁邊是正常造血細胞，符合 ALCL 浸潤骨髓。
features: Single very large atypical cell, several times the size of surrounding granulocytic precursors
Abundant grey-blue cytoplasm filled with numerous clear vacuoles of variable size
Large, slightly irregular nucleus with coarsely granular chromatin and a distinct nucleolus
Moderate N:C ratio; no cytoplasmic granules or engulfed cells
Background of maturing neutrophils (bands, metamyelocytes), myelocytes and red cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows maturing granulocytic and erythroid elements with an admixed markedly enlarged atypical cell. The cell has abundant grey-blue cytoplasm with numerous clear vacuoles and a large, irregular nucleus with coarse chromatin and a visible nucleolus. There is no evidence of phagocytosed cells to suggest a histiocyte. Because such cells may be sparse in marrow involvement, CD30 and ALK immunohistochemistry on the biopsy is recommended. Findings are consistent with marrow involvement by anaplastic large cell lymphoma.

ddx.vs: Metastatic tumor cells typically form cohesive clusters and express keratin or myogenin/desmin, whereas ALCL cells are single and CD30+/ALK+.
Histiocytes have a small oval nucleus with fine chromatin and often contain phagocytosed material, unlike this large nucleolated nucleus without ingested cells.
Burkitt cells are medium-sized and monotonous with deep blue vacuolated cytoplasm, while ALCL cells are much larger and pleomorphic.
Hodgkin cells show very large inclusion-like nucleoli and lack cytoplasmic vacuoles, with CD15+/PAX5 weak and ALK-negative phenotype.
